Set the parameters of a gcTMB fit

Source: R/update.R
update.gcTMB.Rd

update returns the model with some of its parameters replaced by new values, without fitting it again: the model keeps its structure (fform, rform, model, family, correlation and variance), and

  • fixef sets the coefficients of b1-b5 of fform (including coefficients fixed in the fit);

  • VarCorr the covariance matrices of the random effects of rform;

  • sigma the residual standard deviation, or the dispersion of the other families;

  • corpar the parameters of the correlation structure (rho, or the range and nugget);

  • varpar the parameters of the variance function.

The parameters that are not given keep their estimates, and the random effects are the conditional modes at the new parameters. The result is not a fit: it is moved away from the maximum of the likelihood, e.g. to be the true model of a simulation study (see simulate.gcTMB). The new values are not estimates: the standard errors, the covariance matrix of vcov and the confidence intervals are NA, and converged returns NA. The log-likelihood is that of the data at the new parameters.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
update(
  object,
  fixef = NULL,
  VarCorr = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  corpar = NULL,
  varpar = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

fixef

Named numeric vector or NULL. New values of coefficients of b1-b5, named as in fixef (e.g. "b1:(Intercept)"), or by the parameter (e.g. "b1") for a parameter with a single coefficient. Coefficients fixed in the fit, such as the asymmetry b5 (1 by default), can be set too, e.g. fixef=c(b5=4); they stay fixed. NULL (default) keeps all the coefficients.

VarCorr

List or NULL. New covariance matrices of the random effects, named by the terms as in VarCorr, with the rows and columns in the same order; a single matrix for a model with one random effect term. The terms that are not given keep their covariance matrices, and NULL (default) keeps all of them.

sigma

Numeric or NULL. The new residual standard deviation (gaussian, of log(y) for lognormal), or the dispersion parameter of the other families, as returned by sigma.gcTMB. NULL (default) keeps it.

corpar

Numeric or NULL. New parameters of the correlation structure, as returned by corpars, for a model fitted with a correlation structure: the autocorrelation rho, between 0 and 1 for corCAR1 and between -1 and 1 for corAR1; for corExp and corGaus, a named vector with the new range and/or nugget, e.g. c(range=10, nugget=0.2). NULL (default) keeps them.

varpar

Named numeric vector or NULL. New parameters of the variance function (see varFunc) on their natural scale, named as returned by varpars, e.g. c(power=1) or c(const=2, power=0.5) for varConstPower, or the ratio of a stratum for varIdent; the parameters not given keep their values. NULL (default) keeps them.

...

Not used; other arguments give an error that points to refit.

Value

A gcTMB object.

Details

To fit the model again with other components, e.g. a new fform, rform, correlation, variance, model or family, use refit; the other arguments of gcTMB give an error here. To set parameters of a model with a new component, refit it first and then set the parameters of the new fit, e.g. update(refit(fit, fform=b1 ~ trt), fixef=...), as the coefficients of the new fform are not known before the refit.

To fit the data as well as possible with a chosen value of a parameter, refit with that parameter fixed instead, e.g. refit(fit, correlation=corCAR1(0.8, form=~ time | ID, fixed=TRUE)) for the autocorrelation, or refit(fit, start=c(b5=2)) for the asymmetry, which is fixed by default; the other parameters are then estimated given it, whereas setting it keeps their values. For gaussian models without random effects, the residual standard deviation set by sigma is the value given, without the small-sample correction of gcTMB.

See also

refit to fit the model again with other components.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
# a larger asymptote, an asymmetric curve, and a larger variance of b1
vc <- VarCorr(fit)$Plant_ID
vc[1, 1] <- 2*vc[1, 1]
fit2 <- update(fit, fixef=c(b1=150, b5=4), VarCorr=list(Plant_ID=vc))
fixef(fit2)
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>      150.00000       30.86626       12.84146        4.00000 
VarCorr(fit2)
#> $Plant_ID
#>            b1        b2
#> b1 209.588060 -3.159913
#> b2  -3.159913  6.558684
#> attr(,"stddev")
#>        b1        b2 
#> 14.477156  2.560993 
#> attr(,"correlation")
#>             b1          b2
#> b1  1.00000000 -0.08522823
#> b2 -0.08522823  1.00000000
#> 
#> attr(,"sc")
#> [1] 2.074042
# a weaker autocorrelation of the residuals, the other parameters unchanged
fitc <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25,
              correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | Plant_ID))
corpars(update(fitc, corpar=0.7))
#> rho 
#> 0.7 
# a residual standard deviation proportional to the fitted curve
fitv <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, variance=varPower())
varpars(update(fitv, varpar=c(power=1)))
#> power 
#>     1
